slides.headline: 51% Premium + 6% Rally = 92x P/E Math Trap

slides.title: The Retail Illusion vs. Institutional Reality

comparison_data.myth: Retail belief: 'The stock is rallying, it's a winner, I need to buy now before it hits the moon.'
comparison_data.reality: Institutional truth: 'The stock is priced at 46.5x FY26 P/E, leaving zero margin of safety. We are offloading into retail liquidity.'

slides.title: The Hidden Cost of Chasing Momentum

stat_data.label: compounding loss / penalty
stat_data.context: Chasing a 6% rally on a stock already trading at a 51% premium forces you to buy at the peak of institutional distribution. This creates a negative expectancy trade where the downside risk far outweighs the limited upside potential.

slides.title: The Liquidity Trap: How You Get Stuck
flowchart_data: 1. Institutional anchor investors exit at the 51% premium.
2. Retail FOMO drives the additional 6% rally, providing exit liquidity.
3. Price stabilizes as institutional selling exhausts the retail buyer pool.

slides.title: Mathematical Drag: Priced for Perfection
slides.card_text: At 46.5x FY26 P/E, the market has already baked in years of aggressive growth. Any minor earnings miss or sector correction will result in a violent P/E compression, effectively vaporizing the premium you paid at entry.

slides.title: The Non-Negotiable Institutional Rule
slides.card_text: Never chase a stock trading at >40x forward P/E post-listing. The golden rule is to wait for the 'lock-in expiry' volatility window. This is when the true price discovery occurs, often revealing a much more attractive entry point for long-term capital.
